Updates the Ride Owner requirements documentation to reflect a manual join-request workflow: Riders submit requests, and Ride Owners accept or reject them.

Changes
- Expanded Ride Owner user stories from 4 to 15.
- Replaced automatic rider joining with:

  - Rejecting requests

- Reclassified and expanded functional and non-functional requirements.
- Rebuilt the traceability matrix to connect user requirements, functional requirements, use cases, user stories, verification methods, and future Jira/test artifacts.
- Updated AI-agent requirements to confirm that AI does not make join decisions; Ride Owners retain final approval authority.

Key Behaviour Change

## Jira issue

[CS455-14](https://cs455project.atlassian.net/browse/CS455-14): Scaffold web app (Next.js, TypeScript), a sub-task of CS455-12 "Authentication and web pages".

## What and why

Sets up the web app that the homepage, landing, login and registration pages (CS455-15 to 18) are built on, so we all start from the same stack, design system and quality gates.

- **Workspace:** npm workspaces at the root. `apps/web` was generated by create-next-app 16.3.8 (Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, TypeScript strict). The generator output is its own commit, so you can see what was generated and what was written.
- **Design system ("Timetable"):** IBM Plex Sans and Plex Mono, a warm off-white paper background, one deep-green accent for actions, 2px corners, and borders instead of shadows. Tailwind's default palette, shadows, blur, large radii and animations are removed from the theme, so they can't be used by accident.
- **Shared components:** `Button`, `Field`, `Skeleton` and `LoadingRegion` in `src/components/ui/`, plus plain 404 and error pages.
- **Tests:** Vitest with React Testing Library and an 80 % coverage gate. They include a design-rules check (no em dashes, emoji, icon kits, gradients, shadows, blur, large radii, hover animations, coloured left stripes or pure white) and a WCAG contrast check of the colour tokens.
- **CI** on every pull request and push to `master`: format, lint, type-check, tests, build. Plus this PR template.
- **Docs:** `apps/web/README.md` covers the commands, layout, planned routes and design rules. The root README now describes the D1 design.

## For the reviewer

- Please read the **Design rules** in `apps/web/README.md`; Login and Registration (CS455-17, 18) follow them too.
- Check that the `Field` and `Button` APIs suit the login and registration forms.
- Planned routes: `/login` and `/register` are reserved for CS455-17 and 18.

## Requirements addressed

- **NFR-RD-15:** usable at 360 px width; every text colour meets WCAG 2.1 AA (checked by `test/contrast.test.ts`).
- **NFR-RD-17:** TypeScript, at least 80 % coverage, CI rejects changes below it.
- **NFR-RO-USE-01:** buttons and inputs are at least 44 px tall.

## How it was tested

- [x] Unit tests added: 67 tests, 100 % statements, branches, functions and lines. The design-rule checker has its own tests for each banned pattern and for the allowed cases.
- [ ] Integration tests: not applicable yet (no API).
- [x] Checked manually: `npm run dev` renders the placeholder page with the Plex fonts on the paper background, and the route icon in the tab.
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` pass locally. `npm run build` could not run on my laptop (out of memory); it passes in CI.

## Checklist

- [x] Branch name and commits carry the Jira key (`CS455-14`)
- [x] CI passes, including the production build
- [x] UI changes follow the design rules in `apps/web/README.md`
- [x] No secrets, API keys or personal data committed
- [x] Traceability matrix and docs updated if a requirement's status changed (no requirement changed status)
- [ ] Any AI assistance for this change is recorded in the AI Engineering Log (D2 entry to follow)

## Jira issue

[CS455-15](https://cs455project.atlassian.net/browse/CS455-15): Homepage, role-aware home screen and navigation shell, a sub-task of CS455-12 "Authentication and web pages".

## What and why

The signed-in part of the app now has a frame and a starting page for each role.

- **Roles:** `student` (one account both finds and offers rides, as in the D0 proposal) and `admin` (operations admins).
- **Session layer** (`src/lib/session.ts`), following the Next.js data access layer pattern: `getSession()` returns the signed-in user, and `verifySession()` redirects to `/login` when nobody is signed in. Every signed-in page calls it first. The layout only displays the session, because layouts are not re-rendered on navigation.
- **Development sign-in until CS455-17:** under `npm run dev`, `DEV_SESSION_ROLE=student|admin` (and an optional `DEV_SESSION_EMAIL`) in `apps/web/.env.local` signs you in. Production builds and tests ignore it, and a test proves that.
- **Navigation shell:**
  - The header shows the product name, the navigation for the role (with the current page marked for screen readers) and who is signed in, with a skeleton while it loads.
  - The footer links to the terms of service and privacy policy.
  - All routes are defined once, in `src/lib/routes.ts`.
- **`/home`:**
  - Students get "Find a ride" and "Offer a ride", a table of upcoming rides and the join requests waiting for a decision.
  - Admins get a "needs attention" table (SOS incidents, complaints, AI recommendations) and configuration links.
  - There is a loading skeleton. The data comes from `src/lib/home-data.ts`, which returns empty lists and "Not available yet" counts until the rides and admin APIs exist.
- **Design rules:** the automated check now also catches checkmark and sparkle characters, "It's not X, it's Y" phrasing, arbitrary colours and CSS gradients. A literal em dash that had slipped into the CS455-14 rule file is now an escape.
- **Accessibility:** the root layout no longer wraps pages in `<main>`, so the skip link lands after the navigation.

## For the reviewer (Prithviraj)

- **For CS455-17:** login replaces only the body of `getSession()`, and the `Session` type (`userId`, `email`, `displayName`, `role`) is the contract the pages use.
- **Links to planned pages:** links to pages that don't exist yet (`/login`, `/rides`, `/notifications`, admin pages) show the 404 page until their owners build them. The team agreed to link all planned routes.
- **How to view it:** copy `apps/web/.env.example` to `apps/web/.env.local`, set `DEV_SESSION_ROLE`, restart `npm run dev` and open `/home`.

## Requirements addressed

- **D0 / handout §2:** two roles with separate dashboards (student home, admin home).
- **SYS-FR-39:** pages require a signed-in user; the admin screen is only shown for the admin role.
- **Groundwork:**
  - **FR-RD-06.4:** accepted rides appear in the student's upcoming rides.
  - **FR-RD-06.10 and FR-RO-05.1:** request states and the owner's pending requests.
  - **OA-FR-18 and OA-FR-34:** the admin queues.
- **NFR-RD-15:** works at 360 px; the contrast test still passes.
- **NFR-RO-USE-01:** the action buttons are 44 px tall.

## How it was tested

- [x] Unit tests: 121 tests, 100 % statements, branches, functions and lines. They cover the session stub (including production ignoring it), the route map, navigation, the header, footer, both home screens, the page's role switch and redirect, the loading skeleton and the extended design rules.
- Integration tests: not applicable yet (no API).
- [x] Checked on a running dev server:
  - signed out, `/home` streams only the skeleton and then redirects to `/login` (none of the page content is sent);
  - as a student and as an admin, the right screen, navigation and footer render.
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` pass locally; CI runs the build.

## Checklist

- [x] Branch name and commits carry the Jira key (`CS455-15`)
- [x] CI passes, including the production build
- [x] UI changes follow the design rules in `apps/web/README.md`
- [x] No secrets, API keys or personal data committed
- [x] Traceability matrix and docs updated if a requirement's status changed (no requirement changed status)
- [ ] Any AI assistance for this change is recorded in the AI Engineering Log (D2 entry to follow)

commits.headline: CS455-15: Add session access layer, roles and route map
commits.body:
src/lib/session.ts follows the Next.js data access layer pattern: getSession() returns the signed-in user and verifySession() redirects to /login when nobody is signed in. Sign-in itself is CS455-17, so for now getSession() only knows a development user: under next dev, DEV_SESSION_ROLE=student or admin in apps/web/.env.local signs you in with that role. Production builds and tests ignore it, so it cannot act as a backdoor; tests check this.

Roles follow D0: one student account finds and offers rides, and operations admins are separate accounts (src/lib/roles.ts). src/lib/routes.ts keeps every route the app links to in one place, with the main navigation for each role. server-only is added so server modules cannot be bundled into the browser; tests replace it with an empty module. apps/web/.env.example documents the development role.

commits.headline: CS455-15: Add navigation shell with role-based header and legal footer
commits.body:
The (app) route group layout renders the header, the main landmark and a footer. The header shows the product name, the main navigation for the signed-in user's role (students: Home, Find a ride, Offer a ride, Notifications; admins: Home, Incidents, Complaints, Configuration) with aria-current on the current page, and who is signed in. It only reads the session for display; each page checks access itself, as the Next.js guide recommends, because layouts are not re-rendered on navigation. A skeleton header is shown while the session loads.

The footer links to the terms of service and privacy policy pages. The root layout no longer wraps pages in <main>: the skip link now lands after the header, and public pages render their own main landmark.

commits.headline: CS455-15: Add role-aware home screens
commits.body:
/home checks the session with verifySession() and shows students or operations admins their own screen. Students get the two entry points, Find a ride and Offer a ride (D0: one account both rides and offers rides), a table of upcoming rides (IST departure, destination, their part, seats left) and the join requests waiting for a decision, sent or received. Admins get a table of the queues that need attention (SOS incidents, complaints, AI recommendations) and links to configuration. Lists and tables are used rather than feature cards, and a skeleton in the shape of the page is shown while it loads.

src/lib/home-data.ts defines the data the screens need. The rides and admin APIs do not exist yet, so it returns empty lists for students and null counts for admins, shown as 'Not available yet' rather than a false zero; the owners of those features replace only this file. Departures are formatted in IST with tabular digits. ButtonLink reuses the Button styles for links that act as actions.

commits.headline: CS455-15: Extend the design-rule check to more banned patterns
commits.body: Re-checking the design rules found patterns the CS455-14 check missed. It now also fails on checkmark and sparkle characters, the "It's not X, it's Y" phrasing, gradients written as CSS functions inside arbitrary values (radial orbs, dot grids) and arbitrary colours such as text-[#ff00ff], which would bring back neon, pastel or purple colouring outside the tokens. Each new rule has tests for what it flags and what it allows. The em dash in the rule and the dashes in its test data are now written as escapes, so the source contains none of the characters it bans.

commits.headline: CS455-15: Document routes, roles and the development sign-in
commits.body: apps/web/README.md now lists every route with its status, explains the roles, how signed-in pages check access with verifySession(), how to use DEV_SESSION_ROLE until sign-in exists, the main landmark convention and the extended design-rule check. The root README adds the step that copies the example environment file.

commits.headline: CS455-15: Let the development session use a configured email
commits.body: The session now carries the account's email address. Under next dev, the optional DEV_SESSION_EMAIL in apps/web/.env.local sets it, lower-cased and checked to look like an address, and the user is shown by the part before the @, as a new account would be before its profile is set up. Without it, the stub keeps its test-student or test-admin defaults. No password is involved: sign-in is still CS455-17, and passwords and personal addresses stay out of the repository. Test fixtures use example.org addresses.

## Jira issue

[CS455-16](https://cs455project.atlassian.net/browse/CS455-16): Landing page, a sub-task of CS455-12 "Authentication and web pages".

## What and why

The public front page is built, and the first pages looked too plain, so the design system has been refreshed for every page.

- **Landing page (`/`):**
  - A hero with the product's purpose and a live fare calculator on an example ride. The calculator runs the real fare-split code, not a mock-up.
  - The destination hubs, how a ride works, safety and privacy, and a closing call to action. All copy is taken from the D1 requirements, and there are no invented numbers or testimonials.
  - Signed-in users see "Go to your rides" instead of "Register".
- **Fare split** (`src/lib/fare.ts`):
  - `splitFare()` implements Table T-2: whole-rupee shares that always add up to the total, with the owner first in line for the extra rupee.
  - `estimateShare()` is the pre-request estimate of FR-RD-08.1. The ride pages will reuse both.
- **Design refresh:**
  - Forest green with one coral accent, Manrope for text with IBM Plex Mono for fares and times, and two corner sizes (8px controls, 16px panels).
  - A dark colour scheme that follows the device setting.
  - Still no shadows, gradients, icon kits or animations.
- **Shell in the root layout:** the header and footer now appear on every page, public ones included. Signed out, the header shows "Sign in" and "Register".
- **Guardrails:** the design-rule check allows exactly the two corner sizes, and the contrast test checks every text, button and border pairing in both colour schemes.

## For the reviewer (Prithviraj)

- **For CS455-17 and CS455-18:**
  - Pages now get the header, `<main>` and footer from the root layout, so a page renders only its content.
  - Use `Field`, `Button` and `ButtonLink`. The new `accent` variant is for buttons on a forest panel, and a forest panel needs `data-surface="brand"` so focus rings stay visible.
  - Tokens and rules are in `apps/web/README.md`.
- **If your branch started from master before this PR:**
  - `AppHeader` is now `SiteHeader`, and `src/app/(app)/layout.tsx` is gone.
  - Primary actions use `bg-primary` (`accent` is now the coral).
  - `rounded-sm` no longer exists; use `rounded-control`.
- **How to view it:**
  - Run `npm run dev` and open `/`.
  - With `DEV_SESSION_ROLE` set in `apps/web/.env.local` you see the signed-in version. Remove that line to see what visitors see.
  - Switch your system to dark mode to check the dark scheme.

## Requirements addressed

- **D0 / handout:** a public landing page for the service.
- **FR-RD-08.4 and Table T-2:** fare shares in whole rupees that add up to the total. **FR-RD-08.1:** the estimate.
- **SYS-FR-09:** the initial destination hubs are listed.
- **Copy grounded in D1:**
  - P-06, FR-RD-08.3 and FR-RD-09.1: lock time, fixed shares and pool chat.

The production CSP in `next.config.ts` allows fonts only from fonts.gstatic.com, so the self-hosted next/font files were blocked and these pages fell back to Arial. The stylesheet link comes from a client component, so pages outside the design system never fetch or preload it.

The database and the shared rules for rating the people on a completed ride. First sub-task of the Review page story; nothing on screen changes yet.

- `rides.completed_at` (`db/schema.sql`): when the owner marked the ride completed. Rating is open for 72 hours from then (P-16).

## Summary

The API that stores ratings: the people on a completed ride rate each other, within 72 hours, once each. Third sub-task of the Review page story; the page that uses it comes in CS455-43.

> **Merge #36 (CS455-40) first.** This branch starts from it, so until #36 is merged this PR also shows its commit. Review only the CS455-42 commit. It does not depend on #37, and the two merge without conflicts in either order.

### Changes

- `POST /api/rides/[id]/ratings` (`src/app/api/rides/[id]/ratings/route.ts`):
  - body `{ ratings: [{ occupantId, score, comment? }] }`, checked by `parseRatingsRequest()` from #36 (score 1 to 5, comment up to 500 characters, at most 10, no duplicates);
  - `occupantId` is a **seat** on the ride (`riders.id`), never a user ID, so the review page will never need user IDs in the browser (FR-RD-02.4);
  - all ratings in a request are stored, or none of them;
  - answers 201 `{ rated: n }` and nothing else: no IDs, scores or who rated whom.
- Refusals, as `{ error, code }`:

  | Code | Status | Case |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `unauthenticated` | 401 | Not signed in |
  | `not_found` | 404 | Bad ID, or no seat on the ride |
  | `invalid_ratings` | 400 | The body fails the rules |
  | `self_rating` | 400 | Rating yourself |
  | `not_on_ride` | 400 | A seat from another ride |
  | `not_completed`, `cancelled` | 409 | The ride cannot be rated |
  | `closed` | 409 | Past the 72 hours (US-RD-28 AC1) |
  | `already_rated` | 409 | Anyone in the request was already rated (AC2) |

- `src/lib/ride-ratings.ts`:
  - `submitRatings()` locks the rater's own seat, so two requests from one person run one after the other, then inserts everything in one statement. The `ride_ratings` constraints from #36 check again in the database;
  - `getRatingPage()` gives the review page (CS455-43) the ride, whether rating is open, and everyone else on the ride by seat, with whom the viewer has already rated.
- Rate limit `guard('rate-ride', 60, 900)`, higher than the others because many students share one campus IP.

## Jira

Related tickets:

- [CS455-42](https://cs455project.atlassian.net/browse/CS455-42) (story [CS455-39](https://cs455project.atlassian.net/browse/CS455-39))

## Testing

- 550 tests pass locally (29 new; `ride-ratings.ts` fully covered); format, lint, typecheck and build pass.
- On Docker with seeded accounts (SQL, so no email was sent), each refusal in the table came back with its status and code, plus a cross-site request (403).
- Successful requests: 201, and a request mixing a new and an already rated person stored nothing.
- Rating at 80 hours after completion was refused; at 71 h 50 min it went through.

Needs PR 1.

**What it adds**
- `POST /api/rides/[id]/trip` with `{ to }`: the owner starts pickup (once locked), starts the trip, or completes the ride.
  - Starting the trip counts riders not yet marked as on board.
  - Completing stores the final shares.
  - Riders get `trip_update`.
- `POST /api/rides/[id]/arrivals`: during pickup, the owner marks a rider arrived, not arrived or a no-show.
  - A no-show is allowed from 5 minutes after the rider's estimated pickup time; before that the answer is 409 `grace_period` with `availableAt`.
  - The rider is told (`no_show_recorded`), leaves the fare split, and can report it for 7 days.
- `POST /api/rides/[id]/check-in`: a rider says they are at their pickup point.
- `GET /api/rides/[id]/trip`: a stamp, so open pages can refresh when the trip changes.
- **Behaviour change:** `POST /api/rides/[id]/complete` is now the same step as completing through the trip API, so a ride can be completed only once pickup has started (D1 FR-RO-09.4).
- **Knock-on changes:**
  - shares skip no-shows;
  - ratings leave out people who left and no-shows (FR-RO-12.2);
  - the admin rider record marks no-shows.

**Tested**
- Unit and route tests.
- An end-to-end script on Docker: 30 checks covering refusals, grace period, shares, final shares, ratings and the complaint window.
title: CS455-62: Add the trip state, arrival and no-show APIs

commits.headline: CS455-62: Add the trip state, arrival and no-show APIs
commits.body:
src/lib/trip.ts runs each change inside one transaction with the ride
locked, through runTripChange() in src/lib/trip-api.ts:
- POST /api/rides/[id]/trip {to}: the owner starts pickup (once locked),
  starts the trip, or completes the ride. Leaving pickup marks riders not
  yet marked as on board; completing writes ride_final_shares. Riders get
  a trip_update notification. Repeating the current step changes nothing.
- POST /api/rides/[id]/arrivals {occupantId, status}: during pickup the
  owner marks a seat arrived, not arrived or a no-show. A no-show is
  allowed from 5 minutes after the rider's estimated pickup time (409
  grace_period with availableAt before that); the rider is told
  (no_show_recorded) and leaves the fare split.
- POST /api/rides/[id]/check-in: a rider is at their pickup point, from
  the lock until the trip starts.
- GET /api/rides/[id]/trip: {state, stamp} for people on the ride, so the
  page can refresh when the trip changes.
- POST /api/rides/[id]/complete is now the same step as to: 'completed',
  so a ride can be completed only once its trip has started.

Knock-on changes:
- ride-view.ts: shares skip no-shows (activeShares), each person has a
  seat ID and pickup status, and RideView.trip carries the itinerary and
  what the viewer may do. People who left are no longer listed.
- Ratings: seats that left or were no-shows neither rate nor are rated.
- Complaints: a no-show opens the 7-day complaint window for that rider.
- The admin rider record marks rides where the rider was a no-show.
- completeRideRefusal moves from rating-rules.ts to trip-rules.ts.

Rebased on #55 (join requests), keeping both:
- Fares: before the lock the fare is split between the seats still in the
  pool; from the lock each seat keeps its locked_share, a rider who left
  after the lock still owes theirs, and a no-show's share is spread over
  the riders still in the pool, so the shares always add up to the fare.
  The ride page and the final shares both use this.
- Starting pickup applies the lock first if it is due (applyDueLock), and
  an early lock by the owner (rides.locked_at) lets pickup start.
- A no-show ends the rider's accepted request as no_show

## Jira issue

[CS455-86](https://cs455project.atlassian.net/browse/CS455-86) · Debug: fix D1 bugs and loopholes

## What and why

Ten bugs and loopholes where the app did not do what D1 requires, found in a review of everything except the AI chatbot, each fixed with tests. Nothing is redesigned: every fix builds on the existing code, and the files are named below so each owner can check their part. A code review of the first version found problems in some of the fixes; those are fixed too (see "After code review" below).

| # | Bug | Requirement | Fix | Files (owner) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | One person could be in two pools at once: someone offering a ride could request and be accepted on another ride departing within 2 hours, and someone holding a seat could offer an overlapping ride. | FR-RD-06.2, FR-RO-03.2, P-08, T-1 | One rule, `travelConflict()`: a seat held on another unfinished ride (an owner holds a seat on their own ride), not left and not a no-show, departing within 2 hours. Requesting, accepting, offering, editing and leaving all use it. Offering or moving a ride also withdraws the owner's own waiting requests within 2 hours, telling those owners, as acceptance already does (FR-RD-06.8). | `join-requests.ts`, `requests/route.ts` (Mahir); `api/rides/route.ts` (Khushi) |
| 2 | A suspended rider could keep posting in pool chats. | FR-RD-01.5 | Both send paths (the socket in `server.mjs` and `ride-chat.ts`) use one decision, `chatSendRefusal()`: a suspended rider is refused, told until when and why. The ride's owner is not refused: their existing ride keeps running and its riders rely on the chat. The suspension rule and its wording now live once, in `suspension-rule.mjs`, which the socket server can load too. | `server.mjs`, `ride-chat-realtime.mjs`, `ride-chat.ts`, `join-requests.ts` (Mahir); `suspension-rule.mjs`, `suspensions.ts`, `enforcement-rules.ts`, `enforcement.ts`, `Dockerfile`, `docker.yml` |
| 3 | A pool chat was deleted after 30 days even while a complaint citing its messages was unresolved, unless it was a legacy chat report. The cascade also deleted the complaint's links to those messages. | FR-RD-09.5 | Both deletions (the 30 s maintenance and the lazy one) use one rule, `CHAT_KEPT_FOR_COMPLAINT_SQL`: keep the chat while an open chat report, or an unresolved complaint citing one of its messages, exists. A complaint that cites no message does not keep it. | `server.mjs`, `ride-chat-realtime.mjs`, `ride-chat.ts` (Mahir) |
| 4 | `PATCH /api/admin/chat-reports` changed state with no audit record, no same-origin check or rate limit, and worked for the development test admin. The admin pages no longer link to it, but it was still live. | SYS-FR-45, SYS-FR-48, SYS-NFR-03, SYS-NFR-06 | Uses `requireAdminApi` and runs inside `withAdminAction` (action `chat_report.resolve`), so each attempt is audited and the change commits with its audit row. | `api/admin/chat-reports/route.ts`, `ride-chat.ts` (Mahir); `admin-activity.ts`, `home-data.ts` |
| 5 | A rider who left a ride before it ran could still file trip complaints after it completed, and was listed on the complaint form. | FR-RD-13.1 | `leftBeforeTrip()`: someone who left owing nothing was not part of the trip, so a trip complaint is not theirs to file or to answer. A late leaver, who still owes their locked share (FR-RD-07.3), can complain and be complained about, a Payment complaint included. Reporting a chat message is unchanged. | `complaint-rules.ts`, `complaints.ts`, `complaint-queries.ts` |
| 6 | The public completed-trip count included rides the person was a no-show on (and, on their profile, rides they left). Ride history offered a Rate link to someone who had left, which the API then refused. | FR-RD-02.4, FR-RD-12.2 | Counts exclude left and no-show seats; `canRate` is false for someone who left. | `ride-view.ts`; `profile-data.ts` (Mahir) |
| 7 | Editing a ride did not apply the 3-hour maximum departure window that offering one does. | Ride rules, NFR-RD-10 | `editRideForOwner` applies the same limit; an invalid edited window is answered 400 `invalid_departure`, not 409. | `join-requests.ts`, `api/rides/[id]/route.ts` (Mahir) |
| 8 | Deleting an account anonymised it whatever it was doing: riders were left on a ride whose owner could never sign in again, and waiting requests stayed in owners' queues. | FR-RD-16.3 | Deletion is refused (409 `active_rides`, saying what to do first) while the person holds a seat (their own ride included) on a ride under way or whose departure window is not over, or has a waiting request. The slow password hash now runs only when deletion goes ahead. | `api/profile/delete/route.ts` (Mahir) |
| 9 | After itinerary drift, a rider's reconfirmation put the request back to Pending silently, so the owner was never told it was waiting for them again. | S-2 (FR-RD-06.5, 06.6) | The owner gets a `join_request` notification, as already happens when the rider declines. | `join-requests.ts` (Mahir) |
| 10 | An owner could not cancel a ride once its departure time had passed, even though the trip had not started (the ride page says cancellation is available until pickup starts). | FR-RO-04.4, FR-RD-06.11 | A Scheduled ride can be cancelled, and started, until its departure window ends; after that it did not run, and both are refused with `window_over`. A trip under way is never cut off. The owner's manage panel is hidden once the window is over. | `join-requests.ts`, `api/rides/[id]/route.ts`, `RideManagementControls.tsx` (Mahir); `trip-rules.ts`, `trip.ts`, `ride-view.ts` |

## After code review

A code review of the first version raised 15 points. What changed:

- **Cancellation had no upper bound** (#10): an owner could cancel a ride weeks after it ran, wiping the shares fixed at lock. Cancelling and starting now end with the departure window, the same point account deletion uses.
- **No-show seats blocked offering a ride, and offering left the owner's own waiting requests pending** (#1): fixed by the single `travelConflict()` rule and `withdrawRequestsNearOwnRide()`. The rule was written six ways before; the hard-coded 7200 s is gone.
- **Late leavers who still owe could not be complained about** (#5): fixed by `leftBeforeTrip()`.
- **Chats were kept for complaints that never cite them** (#3): now only for complaints citing a message. The lazy deletion's "deleted" check also works now (it returns the row).
- **Suspended owners could not use their own ride's chat; three copies of the suspension rule; the chat refusal had no end date** (#2): owner exemption, one shared rule and wording, and a test that keeps the wording in step with the app's formatter and labels.
- **Over-long edit window answered 409** (#7): now 400. **Deletion hashed before checking** (#8): now after.
- **Jira traceability:** every commit now carries CS455-86. The branch keeps the name `debug`, because GitHub cannot change an open PR's branch.
- **Not changed:**
  - The socket path's call to `chatSendRefusal()` lives in `server.mjs`, which unit tests cannot load. The shared function is unit-tested, and the Docker run below covers the live path.
  - Account deletion keeps Mahir's limit of 3 attempts per hour.

## Requirements addressed

FR-RD-01.5, FR-RD-02.4, FR-RD-06.2, FR-RD-06.5, FR-RD-06.6, FR-RD-06.8, FR-RD-06.11, FR-RD-07.3, FR-RD-09.5, FR-RD-12.2, FR-RD-13.1, FR-RD-16.3, FR-RO-03.2, FR-RO-04.4, SYS-FR-45, SYS-FR-48, SYS-NFR-03, SYS-NFR-06, NFR-RD-10, P-08, T-1, S-2.

## How it was tested

- [x] Unit tests added or updated: every fix has tests; 1331 tests pass, coverage 88.5% statements, 83.6% branches. Lint (0 warnings), typecheck and format all pass.
- [x] Integration tests added or updated: 53 end-to-end checks on a fresh Docker stack built from this branch (fresh database, mail switched off, test users made by SQL), all passing. They cover every fix against real PostgreSQL, including both chat retention paths, a suspended rider and a suspended owner sending over the live socket, and the departure-window bound.
- [x] Checked manually: this branch merges cleanly with master and with #66, and the tests for the touched modules pass on the combined result.

commits.headline: CS455-86: keep each person in one pool at a time
commits.body:
A rider who offered a ride could still request, and be accepted on, another
ride departing within two hours of it, and someone holding a seat on a ride
could offer an overlapping ride of their own (FR-RD-06.2, FR-RO-03.2, P-08).

- Join requests: submitting and accepting now also treat a ride the rider
  offers (scheduled, pickup or in transit) within two hours as a conflict.
  Acceptance rejects with departure_conflict, as in T-1.
- Offering a ride: refused when the owner holds a seat on someone else's
  ride departing within two hours.
- Editing a ride: refused when the new time comes within two hours of a
  seat the owner holds elsewhere.

commits.headline: CS455-86: refuse pool chat messages from suspended members
commits.body:
FR-RD-01.5 says a suspension rejects the rider's pool chat messages from
that moment, but neither the live socket path (server.mjs) nor the library
(ride-chat.ts) checked it, so a suspended rider could keep posting.

- ride-chat-realtime.mjs: senderSuspended(), the active_rider_suspensions
  rule at a given time, and the refusal text. Both send paths use it after
  the membership check; reading the chat stays allowed.
- The suspension notice now lists everything that is refused (offering
  and joining rides, pool chat, ratings) and that SOS stays available.

commits.headline: CS455-86: keep a pool chat while a complaint on its ride is open
commits.body:
FR-RD-09.5 keeps a pool chat past its 30 days while an unresolved
complaint refers to it. Both deletions (the 30 s maintenance in server.mjs
and the lazy one in ride-chat.ts) only looked at open legacy chat reports,
so a complaint filed from the complaint form, even one citing chat
messages, did not stop the chat being deleted, and the cascade then
removed the complaint's links to those messages.

CHAT_KEPT_FOR_COMPLAINT_SQL (ride-chat-realtime.mjs) is now the one rule
both deletions use: an open chat report, or any complaint on the ride
that is not resolved.

commits.headline: CS455-86: audit the legacy chat-report resolve action
commits.body:
PATCH /api/admin/chat-reports changed state without withAdminAction: no
audit record of the attempt or its outcome (SYS-FR-45, SYS-NFR-06), no
same-origin check or rate limit, and the development test admin could
use it. It is no longer linked from the admin pages, but the route is
still live.

- GET and PATCH use requireAdminApi like every other admin route.
- PATCH resolves inside withAdminAction (action chat_report.resolve), on
  the transaction's client, so the change and its audit row commit
  together; resolveChatComplaint() takes an optional client for that.
- The admin home names a chat_report entry by its reference.

commits.headline: CS455-86: keep trip complaints between people who were on the trip
commits.body:
FR-RD-13.1 lets a rider complain about the owner or a co-rider of that
trip. Filing only checked that both people had ever had a seat, so a
rider who left before the ride ran could still file trip complaints
after it completed, and people who had left were listed on the form as
someone to complain about.

- fileComplaint: a trip complaint is refused (not found) from someone
  who left, and (not on ride) about someone who left. A reported chat
  message is unchanged: its sender may have left since.
- The complaint form is not found for a viewer who left, unless they are
  reporting a message, and lists only people who stayed, plus the sender
  of the reported message.

commits.headline: CS455-86: count only trips a person completed, and rate only those
commits.body:
- The public completed-trip count on the ride page (FR-RD-02.4) counted
  rides the person was a no-show on, and the count on their own profile
  also counted rides they had left. Both now count a completed ride only
  when the person neither left it nor was a no-show.
- Ride history showed a Rate link on a completed ride the viewer had
  left before it ran, which the ratings API then refused (FR-RD-12.2).
  canRate is now false for them, as it already was for a no-show.

commits.headline: CS455-86: keep an edited departure window within 3 hours
commits.body:
Offering a ride caps the departure window at 180 minutes
(RIDE_RULES.maxWindowMinutes), but editing it only checked that the start
was before the end and before the lock, so an owner could stretch a ride's
window to days after riders had joined. editRideForOwner now applies the
same limit.

commits.headline: CS455-86: refuse account deletion while others rely on the account
commits.body:
Deleting an account anonymised it and removed its sessions and profile,
whatever it was doing. Someone owning an upcoming ride left its riders on
a ride whose owner could never sign in again, a rider's seat stayed
taken, and their waiting requests stayed in owners' queues
(FR-RD-16.3 keeps what unresolved obligations need).

The account row is now locked first, and deletion is refused (409
active_rides, with what to do) while the person holds a seat, their own
ride included, on a ride under way or scheduled with its window not over,
or has a request waiting for an owner's decision.

commits.headline: CS455-86: tell the owner when a rider reconfirms changed terms
commits.body:
After itinerary drift (FR-RD-06.5), a rider's reconfirmation put the
request back to Pending silently, so the owner, who could not accept it
until then, was never told it was waiting again. S-2 lists "owner
notified of the outcome" for both answers; declining already did. The
owner now gets a join_request notification on reconfirmation too.

commits.headline: CS455-86: let an owner cancel a ride until its trip starts
commits.body:
cancelRideForOwner refused once the departure time had passed, but the
trip starts with Pickup in Progress, not at the clock time (FR-RO-04.4
"a ride that has not started", FR-RD-06.11 "before or after lock time").
The ride page itself says cancellation is available until pickup starts.
An owner whose ride could not run had no way to release its riders, and
the ride stayed Scheduled with their shares locked.

A scheduled ride can now be cancelled at any time; a ride in Pickup in
Progress or In Transit is refused with trip_started, and a completed or
cancelled one with ride_closed, as before.

commits.headline: CS455-86: keep the new owner tests apart from PR #66's
commits.body:
The edit and cancellation tests added for this PR sat where Khushi's
open PR #66 inserts its own test, so the two would conflict. They now
live in their own describe block at the end of the file; the existing
cancellation test keeps its place and only its ride state changes.

commits.headline: CS455-86: one rule for one pool at a time, for joining, offering and …
commits.body:
…editing

Code review of this PR found the P-08 rule written six different ways,
disagreeing at the edges: joining and accepting looked at accepted
requests, offering a ride counted no-show seats and hard-coded 7200 s,
and an owner could offer two rides 30 minutes apart. Offering a ride also
left the owner's own waiting requests near it pending, though they could
no longer be accepted.

- travelConflict() in join-requests.ts is now the one rule: a seat the
  person holds on another unfinished ride (their own ride's included),
  not left and not a no-show, departing within REQUEST_CONFLICT_WINDOW_MS.
  Requesting, accepting, offering, editing, leaving and the drift
  exemption all use it; ownsRideNear and acceptedRideConflict are gone.
- withdrawRequestsNearOwnRide(): offering a ride, or moving one, withdraws
  the owner's own waiting requests within two hours (reason
  own_ride_offered) and tells those owners, as acceptance already does
  (FR-RD-06.8). Mahir's withdrawConflictingRequests takes the reason and
  message as a parameter for this.

commits.headline: CS455-86: end cancelling and starting a ride with its departure window
commits.body:
Code review: allowing cancellation of any Scheduled ride had no upper
bound. Nothing moves an elapsed ride out of Scheduled, so an owner could
cancel a ride weeks after it ran (if they never pressed Start pickup),
wiping the shares fixed at lock and telling riders they owe nothing. The
same ride could also still be started weeks later, making shares due for
a trip nobody took, and account deletion already treated it as over.

One definition now: a Scheduled ride is still to happen until its
departure window ends.
- cancelRideForOwner refuses after departure_end (409 window_over, with a
  message); before that, cancelling until pickup starts is unchanged.
- tripTransitionRefusal takes the window end and refuses Start pickup
  after it (window_over); a trip already under way is never cut off.
- The owner's manage panel is hidden once the window is over.

commits.headline: CS455-86: keep complaints possible about late leavers who still owe
commits.body:
Code review: limiting trip complaints to people who stayed also shut out
riders who left after the lock. They are the only leavers who still owe
money (their locked share stays payable, FR-RD-07.3), so an owner could
not file a Payment complaint about an unpaid late cancellation, and the
form no longer listed them.

leftBeforeTrip() in complaint-rules.ts is now the one rule: someone who
left owing nothing (before the lock, or on changed terms) was not part of
the trip. A late leaver, whose seat keeps its locked_share, can complain
and be complained about, and is listed on the form.

commits.headline: CS455-86: keep a pool chat only for complaints that cite it
commits.body:
Code review: keeping a chat past 30 days for any unresolved complaint on
its ride also kept it for complaints that never refer to it (a tardiness
complaint, say), possibly indefinitely, though FR-RD-09.5 keeps a chat
only while an unresolved complaint references it.

- CHAT_KEPT_FOR_COMPLAINT_SQL now keeps a chat for an open chat report,
  or an unresolved complaint citing one of its messages
  (complaint_chat_messages, which form complaints with a message and
  mirrored chat reports both use). Existing indexes cover the lookup.
- The lazy deletion in ride-chat.ts returns the deleted row, so its
  "deleted" branch now works instead of always falling through to an
  extra SELECT.

commits.headline: CS455-86: one suspension rule and message, and owners keep their ride…
commits.body:
…'s chat

Code review of the chat suspension check:
- A suspended owner could not post in their own ride's chat, even during
  pickup, when its riders rely on it to coordinate. The owner of the ride
  is now exempt, as for its trip actions: their existing ride keeps
  running. Riders are refused as before (FR-RD-01.5).
- The suspension rule existed three times (suspensions.ts, Mahir's
  hasSuspension, the chat helper) and the chat refusal left out the end
  date and reason category. suspension-rule.mjs now holds the rule
  (ACTIVE_SUSPENSION_SQL) and the wording (suspensionRefusal), loadable by
  the socket server too; suspensions.ts, join-requests.ts and
  enforcement-rules.ts use it. A test keeps its date format and labels
  equal to format.ts and complaint-rules.ts.
- chatSendRefusal() is the one send decision for both paths (server.mjs
  and ride-chat.ts), unit-tested with the owner exemption. The socket
  path itself still runs only in server.mjs; the Docker run covers it.
- The Dockerfile copies suspension-rule.mjs, and the Docker workflow runs
  when it changes.

commits.headline: CS455-86: answer bad edit windows with 400, and hash only real deletions
commits.body:
Code review:
- An edited departure window that is too long, ends before it starts or
  leaves no time before lock is invalid input, but came back as 409
  ride_closed. editRideForOwner now returns invalid_departure, which the
  route answers with 400 and the reason, like its other input checks.
- Account deletion computed the slow replacement-password hash before
  checking whether deletion could go ahead, so every refused attempt paid
  for it. The hash now runs only after the check passes.

commits.headline: CS455-86: list suspension-rule.mjs apart from PR #66's workflow paths
commits.body:
Both PRs added a path right after notification-realtime.mjs in the Docker
workflow, so they would conflict. The line now sits after server.mjs.

Jira: CS455-110 (A1 of the D3 story "Integration and adversarial testing with reports")

## Why

D3 asks for integration and adversarial test reports backed by tests anyone can rerun. Every API test we have mocks the database and the session, so nothing tested the routes against real SQL, constraints and triggers. This PR adds the harness that A2 to A4 (CS455-111 to 113) build on, plus a shared account seed for the Playwright system tests (Story B).

## What it adds

- **`npm run test:integration`** (`apps/web/vitest.integration.config.mts`): calls the real route handlers in-process against a real PostgreSQL database. Only `next/headers` is replaced, by `test/integration/next-headers.ts`, which serves the current test request's headers and cookies. Sessions, the same-origin check, rate limits, SQL constraints and triggers all run exactly as in the app.
- **A fresh database every run, a clean one every test:** the run drops and recreates the database in `TEST_DATABASE_URL` and applies `db/schema.sql`. Before every test all tables are truncated and the schema's own rows (places, hubs, vehicle types, tags) are put back.
- **Safety (fails closed):** the tests touch the database only if all of these hold:
  - its name ends in `_test`;
  - it is on this machine (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `::1`);
  - `ALLOW_TEST_DATABASE_RESET` names exactly that database (an explicit opt-in);
  - it carries the marker global setup writes on the database it creates. An existing database without the marker is never dropped, and every test file checks the marker again before its first reset.

  Mail and Gemini are switched off in the test environment.
- **`test/seed/accounts.ts`** (shared, plain SQL, no app imports): `createAccount` (verified, profile set up) and `createSessionToken`, so no test sends a registration email.
- **`test/integration/http.ts`**: `callRoute(handler, { method, body, params, as, origin, ip })`, returning `{ status, body }`.
- **`test/integration/fixtures.ts`**: `signedInStudent`, `signedInAdmin`, `offerRide` (through `POST /api/rides`) and `moveDeparture` (the same SQL time move setup.md uses to try a trip).
- **Smoke tests** (`harness.int.test.ts`, 6 tests):
  - a ride is offered through the API and read back from the database and the requests route;
  - signed out gives 401, a cross-site POST gives 403, an expired session gives 401;
  - the admin role comes from the database (student 403 `not_admin`, admin 200);
  - `moveDeparture` keeps the window length;
  - a row from one test is gone in the next, while the reference data stays.
- **Unit tests** for every refusal of the database guard (`test/test-database.test.ts`).

## Team files touched (small, additive)

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: a new job, "Integration tests (PostgreSQL)", with a `postgres:16` service. The existing `checks` job is unchanged.
- `apps/web/vitest.config.mts`: excludes `test/integration/**`, so the unit run and its 80% gate are unchanged.
- `apps/web/package.json`: the `test:integration` script.
- `apps/web/setup.md` ("Integration tests") and `apps/web/README.md`: how to run it.

## How to run locally

1. `docker compose up -d db`
2. Add two lines to `apps/web/.env.local`: `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://crp:<POSTGRES_PASSWORD>@127.0.0.1:5433/crp_test` and `ALLOW_TEST_DATABASE_RESET=crp_test`. If an older `crp_test` exists, it is refused (no marker): drop it once with `docker compose exec db dropdb -U crp crp_test`.
3. `npm run test:integration` from `apps/web` (about 3 seconds)

## For Khushi (Playwright, B2/B3)

`test/seed/accounts.ts` takes any `pg` Client or Pool, so the system tests can sign people in without email: create the account, create a session token, set it as the session cookie. The Docker stack runs a production build, so the cookie there is `__Host-crp_session` (Secure, path `/`), not `crp_session`.

## Test evidence

- `npm run test:integration`: 6/6 passed, run three times in a row on the Compose database.
- `TEST_DATABASE_URL=.../crp`: refused before connecting; the `crp` data was untouched.
- `npm run test`: 200 files, 1520 tests passed; coverage 87.47% statements, 80.73% branches, 88.69% functions, 89.81% lines.
- `npm run format:check`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build`: clean.

## Review follow-up (648d4dd)

Khushi pointed out that a name ending in `_test` does not prove the database is disposable. The opt-in, local-host and marker checks above were added for that. Checked against the real database:

- a `crp_test` made before the marker existed: refused before any `DROP`;
- no opt-in, an opt-in naming another database, a hosted host: each refused before connecting;
- a failing marker check in a test file: Vitest skips that file's tests, so no reset runs;
- after a one-off `dropdb`: 6/6 passed on two runs in a row, with the marker present.

Jira: Bug to be created (label `d3-defect`, `found-by-testing`); the key will be added here.

**Stacked on #83** (it needs the integration harness for its regression tests). Merge #83 first.

## The bug

On a real database, **every seat request fails with 500**, and so does the payment reminder scheduler. This has been the case since the settlement commit 2dcae5e (14 Oct).

```
Submit ride request failed: error: operator does not exist: timestamp with time zone < interval
    at submitJoinRequest (src/lib/join-requests.ts:523)
```

Cause: `completed_at < $2 - interval '7 days'` with a JavaScript `Date` as `$2`. node-postgres sends the Date untyped, so Postgres reads `$2 - interval` as interval minus interval, and comparing a timestamptz with an interval has no operator. The unit tests mock the database, so they could not see it.

| Where | Effect |
|---|---|
| `submitJoinRequest()`: overdue-payment check (FR-RD-11) | `POST /api/rides/[id]/requests` always 500: nobody can request a seat |
| `sendDuePaymentReminders()` | `POST /api/cron/payment-reminders` always 500: no reminders are sent |

## The fix

Cast the parameter, `$n::timestamptz - interval '...'`, as `complaints.ts` already does. Three lines; no behaviour change apart from the queries working.

## Regression tests (`test/integration/bugs/timestamp-parameters.int.test.ts`)

On a real Postgres, through the real route:
- a rider with nothing unpaid can request a seat (201);
- a share due for more than 7 days still blocks a new request (409 `payment_overdue`), and one due for 6 days does not;
- the 24 h reminder is sent once, then the 72 h one.

**Without the cast, all 4 fail with the Postgres error above; with it, all pass.**

## Checks

- `npm run test:integration`: 10/10 passed.
- `join-requests.test.ts` and `payment-settlement.test.ts`: 41/41 passed.
- Format, lint and typecheck are clean.

Mahir, this touches your settlement code (`join-requests.ts` and `payment-settlement.ts`), only to add the casts.

## Follow-up (fd5b030): the reminder test is now deterministic

The reminder test failed about 1 full run in 12, with "The original final share cannot be changed" (Khushi's comment on #88). The cause was in the test, not the app:

- the seeded shares took `created_at` from Postgres's clock, while the reminder was stamped by the test's clock a millisecond later;
- the container's clock runs about 1 ms ahead, so the reminder could look older than its share, which the share trigger refuses.

The seed now dates the shares from the ride's completion, as `trip.ts` does. With the test clock simulated 1 s behind, the old seed failed 3 of 3 runs and the new one passes 3 of 3.

Jira: Bug to be created (label `d3-defect`, `found-by-adversarial`); the key will be added here.

**Stacked on #83 to #86** (its regression test uses their fixtures). Merge in order; only the last commit is new here.

## The weakness

A seat request sent with an idempotency key that was already used was answered with the request first made with that key, whatever the new request asked for.

| Sent again with the key | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Same ride, same pickup point (a real retry) | 200, the same request | unchanged |
| **Another ride** | 200 "already submitted", the first ride's request; nothing on the ride asked for | 409 `idempotency_key_reused`, nothing created |
| **Another pickup point** (a retry after a lost response, pickup changed) | 200; the change silently dropped | 409 `idempotency_key_reused`, the first request unchanged |

`JoinRequestControls` keeps its key across failed tries, and the same component can stay mounted across client-side navigation, so the UI can send a key again with other details.

## The fix

- `submitJoinRequest()`: a key replays only the request it was first sent with (same ride and pickup point, FR-RD-06.9). Anything else is refused with `idempotency_key_reused`.
- Requests route: the 409 message for that code.
- `JoinRequestControls.tsx`: drops its key on that answer, so the rider's next try gets a key of its own (1 line).

## Tests

- `test/integration/bugs/idempotency-key-reuse.int.test.ts` (real Postgres):
  - another ride: refused;
  - another pickup point: refused;
  - an unchanged retry: still replayed.

  **Without the fix, the first two fail; with it, all pass.**
- `join-requests.test.ts`: the replay mock now carries the ride and pickup point, plus 2 new cases (37/37 pass).
- Integration suite: green. Format, lint and typecheck are clean.

## Review follow-up (32d44c6): simultaneous first uses of one key

Khushi asked whether two first uses of the same unused key could both pass the lookup. They cannot:

- `submitJoinRequest()` runs in one transaction whose first statement locks the rider's `users` row (`FOR UPDATE`). So one rider's submissions run one after another, and a later one sees the earlier one's key.
- The key table's primary key `(rider_id, idempotency_key)` refuses a second claim regardless.

Two tests were added:

- five rounds of four simultaneous first uses of one key, two for each of two rides: one request and one key row; the winning ride's sends get that request (201, then a 200 replay), and the other ride's get 409;
- a second key row inserted directly fails with `23505`.

With the row lock removed, the race test fails (`[201, 409, 500, 500]`).

Mahir, this touches your join request code (`join-requests.ts`, the requests route and `JoinRequestControls.tsx`); the changes are small and additive.

commits.body:
`$n - interval '...'` with a JavaScript Date parameter: node-postgres
sends the Date untyped, so Postgres reads it as interval minus interval
and the comparison with a timestamptz column fails with "operator does
not exist: timestamp with time zone < interval".

- submitJoinRequest (overdue-payment check, added in 2dcae5e): every
  POST /api/rides/[id]/requests answered 500, so nobody could request
  a seat.
- sendDuePaymentReminders: POST /api/cron/payment-reminders failed the
  same way.

Cast the parameter ($n::timestamptz), as complaints.ts already does.
Mocked unit tests could not see this; the new integration tests do:
they fail with the Postgres error without the cast and pass with it.
